subject: Anthropology
title: Special-Purpose Money
description: A short lesson to help you apply Special-Purpose Money.

hook.text: In some cultures, cattle buy brides but can't buy food. One type of money can't do everything. Each has its purpose.

buildup.text: Special-purpose money can only be used for specific transactions — bridewealth, ritual payments, or fines.

discovery.text: Unlike general-purpose money, these currencies keep different social spheres separate. Love and trade don't mix.

twist.text: Modern money is general-purpose. It treats everything as equal — erasing the moral distinctions older systems preserved.

climax.text: Special-purpose money shows that not everything should be for sale. Some values resist being reduced to a price.

punchline.text: Some things are priceless by design.

quiz.question: What is special-purpose money?
options: Currency restricted to specific types of transactions

details.summary: Special-purpose money can only be used within specific exchange spheres — for example, shell money for bridewealth but not food purchases. Unlike general-purpose money, it keeps different types of exchange morally separate, preventing the conversion of all values into a single measure.
details.whyItMatters: Special-purpose money reveals that not all values are commensurable. Some societies deliberately prevent certain things from being purchased with money, maintaining moral boundaries between exchange spheres that general-purpose money erodes.
takeaways: Special-purpose money works only within specific exchange spheres
It keeps different types of exchange morally separate
It prevents the conversion of all values into a single monetary measure

faq.question: What are exchange spheres?
faq.answer: Exchange spheres are ranked categories of goods that can only be exchanged within their own sphere. The Tiv of Nigeria had three spheres: subsistence goods, prestige items, and rights over people. Converting between spheres was morally suspect and socially regulated.

faq.question: Does modern society have anything like special-purpose money?
faq.answer: Gift cards, food stamps, airline miles, and casino chips function as limited-purpose money. More broadly, social norms against monetizing certain things — paying friends for favors, selling organs — represent informal limits on general-purpose money's reach.
